title: 赏牡丹
author: 刘禹锡
intro: Why is the peony called China’s “national beauty”? This little poem compares it with two other flowers and gives the answer — the whole capital comes out to see it.
analysis: 这首诗赞美牡丹，用的是对比和衬托：要夸一样东西，先拿别的来比。第一句说庭院前的芍药虽然艳丽，却缺少风骨；第二句说池塘里的荷花虽然干净，却显得冷淡少情。这两种花本来都很美，诗人故意挑它们的不足，是为了衬托牡丹。第三句直接说：只有牡丹才是真正的“国色”——全国最美的颜色。第四句写效果：牡丹一开，整个京城都轰动了，人人去看。唐代长安人特别爱牡丹，春天赏牡丹是全城的大事。“国色天香”后来成了形容牡丹、也形容美女的成语，今天牡丹仍被很多人看作中国的代表花。
analysisEn: This poem praises the peony through comparison: to show how good something is, first set it beside something else. Line 1 says the herbaceous peony (芍药) in the courtyard is pretty but lacks dignity; line 2 says the lotus in the pond is pure but rather cold and unfeeling. Both flowers are lovely in their own right — the poet picks on their weak points only to make the peony shine. Line 3 states it plainly: only the peony has true “national beauty” (国色), the loveliest colour in the land. Line 4 shows the effect: when the peonies bloom, the whole capital is stirred and everyone goes out to see them. In Tang-dynasty Chang’an, people were crazy about peonies, and spring peony-viewing was a city-wide event; the best plants sold for a fortune. The phrase 国色天香 (“national beauty, heavenly fragrance”) later became an idiom for peonies and for beautiful women, and many people still think of the peony as China’s flower.
background: Liu Yuxi (772–842) was a Tang poet known for his lively quatrains and folk-song style. This poem reflects the peony craze of Chang’an in his day.
pronunciation: 芍药 sháo yào；芙蕖 fú qú；少情 shǎo。机器朗读“蕖”可能读错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字。
version: 采用通行本。“唯有牡丹真国色”一作“惟有”。

lines.py: tíng qián sháo yào yāo wú gé
lines.lit: The herbaceous peonies before the hall are showy but lack dignity;
lines.en: The courtyard’s peonies are pretty, but have no grace;

lines.py: chí shàng fú qú jìng shǎo qíng
lines.lit: the lotus on the pond is pure but has little feeling.
lines.en: the lotus on the pond is pure, but cold.

lines.py: wéi yǒu mǔ dān zhēn guó sè
lines.lit: Only the tree peony is the true beauty of the nation;
lines.en: Only the peony is the true beauty of the land —

lines.py: huā kāi shí jié dòng jīng chéng
lines.lit: when its flowers open, it moves the capital.
lines.en: when it blooms, the whole capital comes out to see.

words.note: 现代汉语也说，和牡丹很像。
古义，现代汉语“妖艳”还用。
古代对荷花的雅称，现代汉语说“荷花”。

words.en: the greatest beauty in the land
words.note: 成语“国色天香”今天仍用。
现代汉语也说，如“清明时节”。
这里指长安；现代汉语也说。

imagery.name: 牡丹
imagery.zh: 牡丹是“真国色”，象征雍容华贵，一开就轰动京城。
imagery.en: The peony is the “true national beauty”, a symbol of richness and splendour that sets the whole capital talking.

imagery.name: 莲
imagery.zh: 荷花在这里被说成“净少情”，用来衬托牡丹的热烈。
imagery.en: Here the lotus is called pure but cold — a foil to set off the peony’s warmth.
